mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over a 3-month window signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1 growth > 3% quarter-over-quarter for two consecutive quarters) signals robust demand expansion, which boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 qoq growth > 3% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained GDPC1 growth > 3% qoq for two quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a broad-based demand recovery, which boosts equity valuations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both above 12-month moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and HOUST exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 200,000 for three consecutive months signals strong labor market momentum, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 200000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained monthly PAYEMS growth above 200,000 for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below their 12-month averages signals a deflationary easing cycle, which increases uncertainty and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both below 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL are below their 12-month averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months.
